title: Nepal puts Tibetan refugee population at over 3,500 - Tibetan Review
description: Nepal puts Tibetan refugee population at over 3,500  Tibetan Review
publisher.title: Tibetan Review
full_article:
(TibetanReview.net, Aug09’26) – The police in Nepal have put the number of Tibetan refugees living in the country at over 3,500, the second largest group after Bhutanese refugees, with the total being over 10,000, reported myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com Aug 7. The report said the police made the figures public after misleading comments and discussions about refugees began circulating on social media.

The report cited police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle as saying 6,272 Bhutanese refugees were currently living in Nepal.

Kafle has put the number of Tibetan refugees living in the country, per police data, at 3,527, followed by 527 Rohingya refugees.

The vast majority of Tibetan refugees living in the country remain unregistered and therefore uncounted. Nepal stopped registering Tibetan refugees decades ago due to pressure from China which insists they are illegal migrants.

The refugees from Bhutan are ethnically Nepali (known as Lhotshampas) and the vast majority of their original total of over 1,00,000 – expelled between 1988 and 1993 – have been resettled in the West, starting in 2007. They were mostly taken in by the United States (85,000 individuals). The other counties included Australia, Canada, United Kingdom, New Zealand, Denmark, and The Netherlands.

The Himalayan kingdom threw them out as illegal migrants and, reportedly, in a political crackdown.

title: 32nd International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples - The Rising Nepal
description: 32nd International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug 9: President Ramchandra Paudel reminded that the country's Constitution has ensured rights to all communities by acknowledging unity in diversity.

Addressing a programme organised by the Indigenous Nationalities Commission on the occasion of the 32nd International Day of the World's Indigenous Peoples, the-Head-of-State said, "Nepal is a country with multi-case, multi-language, multi-religious and multicultural features." The unique identity and culture of the indigenous people who have been living here since ancient times remain as the national pride of Nepal, according to him.

Paudel said, “The indigenous peoples are the children of this land and have a lasting, inner and deeper connection with water, land and natural resources.” The President said it is the government's responsibility to ensure the meaningful participation of indigenous nationalities at the policy and decision-making levels. He added that the latest data shows an encouraging 36.8 percent participation of indigenous communities at the local level.

He said he believed that access to education for these communities should be further increased to promote their overall advancement. Nepal is in the forefront in the international forum in view of the protection and promotion of indigenous rights and it is the first country in the entire South Asia to endorse ILO Convention No 169.

The President, reiterating full commitments to the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples and the Convention on Biological Diversity, said these international documents recognize rights and cultural independence of indigenous nationalities. It is noted that Indigenous and Tribal Peoples Convention, 1989 (No. 169) is a major international treaty adopted by the International Labour Organization (ILO) on June 27, 1989 which exclusively promotes rights, cultures, lands, and the way of life of indigenous and tribal peoples.

Since the establishment of the federal democratic republic system in the country, Nepal has through the Constitution, provisioned for the establishment of the 'Indigenous Nationalities Commission', the President said. He expressed confidence that this constitutional body is championing on the empowerment of indigenous peoples by protecting their glorious history, language, and culture, and that it will continue to play its role more effectively.

According to the President, journey towards a prosperous Nepal will remain incomplete in absence of justice to and rights of indigenous nationalities." National integrity will be further reinforced by addressing remnants of past conflicts and dissatisfactions through democratic dialogues and constitutional procedures and promoting durable peace, maintaining community goodwill and unity."

"We should not forget that rights of all castes, classes and the backward communities have been ensured in democracy," he underscored.

Underlining the need to economically empower the indigenous nationalities through the commercial transformations of their indigenous knowledge, skills and technology, the President pressed the need to pursue a policy of securing economic advantages by connecting indigenous culture to tourism through the implementation of innovative approaches like 'open-air living museum'.(RSS)

काठमांडू, ९ अगस्त : राष्ट्रिय रामचन्द्र पौडेल देशके संविधानमे विविधतामे एकताके स्वीकार करैत सभ समुदायके अधिकार सुनिश्चित कएलगेल स्मरण करौलनि ।

विश्व आदिवासी जनजातिक ३२म अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय दिवसके अवसरमे आदिवासी राष्ट्रियता आयोगद्वारा आयोजित कार्यक्रमके सम्बोधन करैत राष्ट्राध्यक्ष कहलनि जे, नेपाल बहुप्रकरण, बहुभाषी, बहुधार्मिक आ बहुसांस्कृतिक विशेषता वाला देश अछि । प्राचीन काल सँ एतय रहनिहार आदिवासी लोकनिक विशिष्ट पहिचान आ संस्कृति नेपालक राष्ट्रीय गौरवक रूप मे बनल अछि, हुनक अनुसार ।

पौडेल कहलकै, “आदिवासी लोगऽ के ई भूमि के संतान छै आरू पानी, जमीन आरू प्राकृतिक संसाधनऽ स॑ एकरऽ स्थायी, आतंरिक आरू गहरा संबंध छै।” राष्ट्रपति नँ कहलकै कि नीति आरू निर्णय लेबै के स्तर प आदिवासी राष्ट्रीयता के सार्थक भागीदारी सुनिश्चित करना सरकार के जिम्मेदारी छै । हुनी आरू कहलकै कि ताजा आंकड़ा स्थानीय स्तर प आदिवासी समुदाय के उत्साहजनक 36.8 प्रतिशत भागीदारी के दर्शाबै छै ।

हुनी कहलकै कि हुनकऽ मानना ​​छै कि ई समुदायऽ लेली शिक्षा के पहुँच आरू बढ़ाबै के चाही ताकि हुनकऽ समग्र उन्नति बढ़ैलऽ जाय सक॑ । नेपाल आदिवासी अधिकार के संरक्षण आरू संवर्धन के दृष्टि स॑ अंतरराष्ट्रीय मंच म॑ सबसें आगू छै आरू पूरा दक्षिण एशिया म॑ आईएलओ केरऽ कन्वेंशन नंबर १६९ के समर्थन करै वाला ई पहिलऽ देश छेकै ।

राष्ट्रपति न॑ संयुक्त राष्ट्र केरऽ आदिवासी लोगऽ के अधिकारऽ के घोषणापत्र आरू जैविक विविधता महासन्धि के प्रति पूर्ण प्रतिबद्धता क॑ दोहरबैत॑ कहलकै कि ई अंतर्राष्ट्रीय दस्तावेज आदिवासी राष्ट्रीयता के अधिकार आरू सांस्कृतिक स्वतंत्रता क॑ मान्यता दै छै । ध्यान देलऽ जाय छै कि आदिवासी आरू आदिवासी लोगऽ के सम्मेलन, १९८९ (संख्या १६९) अंतर्राष्ट्रीय श्रम संगठन (आईएलओ) द्वारा २७ जून, १९८९ क॑ अपनालऽ गेलऽ एगो प्रमुख अंतर्राष्ट्रीय संधि छै जे विशेष रूप स॑ आदिवासी आरू आदिवासी लोगऽ के अधिकार, संस्कृति, भूमि, आरू जीवनशैली क॑ बढ़ावा दै छै ।

देशमे संघीय लोकतान्त्रिक गणतन्त्र व्यवस्था स्थापना भेलाक बादसँ नेपाल संविधानक माध्यमसँ, ‘आदिवासी राष्ट्रियता आयोग’ स्थापनाक प्रावधान केने राष्ट्रपति बतौलनि । हुनी विश्वास व्यक्त करलकै कि ई संवैधानिक निकाय आदिवासी लोगऽ के गौरवशाली इतिहास, भाषा, आरू संस्कृति के रक्षा करी क॑ ओकरऽ सशक्तिकरण के समर्थन करी रहलऽ छै, आरू ई अपनऽ भूमिका क॑ अधिक प्रभावी ढंग स॑ निभाबै वाला छै ।

राष्ट्रपति के अनुसार आदिवासी राष्ट्रीयता के न्याय आरू अधिकार के अभाव में समृद्ध नेपाल के तरफ यात्रा अपूर्ण रहतै।" लोकतांत्रिक संवाद आरू संवैधानिक प्रक्रिया के माध्यम स॑ विगत के संघर्ष आरू असंतोष के अवशेष के संबोधित करी क॑ स्थायी शांति, सामुदायिक सद्भावना आरू एकता क॑ कायम रखै के साथ राष्ट्रीय अखंडता क॑ आरू मजबूत करलऽ जैतै ।"

ओ एहि बात पर जोर देलनि जे लोकतंत्र मे सब जाति, वर्ग आ पिछड़ल समुदायक अधिकार सुनिश्चित भेल अछि, ई नहि बिसरबाक चाही।

देशी राष्ट्रीयता क॑ ओकरऽ स्वदेशी ज्ञान, कौशल आरू तकनीक के व्यावसायिक रूपांतरण के माध्यम स॑ आर्थिक रूप स॑ सशक्त बनाबै के जरूरत क॑ रेखांकित करतें हुअ॑ राष्ट्रपति न॑ ‘खुला हवा म॑ रहय वाला संग्रहालय’ जैसनऽ अभिनव दृष्टिकोण के कार्यान्वयन के माध्यम स॑ देशी संस्कृति क॑ पर्यटन स॑ जोड़ै के नीति क॑ अपनाबै के जरूरत प॑ दबाव डाललकै ।(आरएसएस)

title: India signs Mutual Legal Assistance Agreement on Criminal Matters with Nepal - newsonair.gov.in
description: India signs Mutual Legal Assistance Agreement on Criminal Matters with Nepal  newsonair.gov.in
publisher.title: newsonair.gov.in
full_article:
An agreement has been reached between India and Nepal on mutual legal assistance on criminal matters. The agreement to this effect was signed by Ambassador of India to Nepal Naveen Srivastava and Nepal’s Joint Secretary at the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Binod Kumar Bhattarai, on behalf of the Government of Nepal.

The agreement on mutual assistance on criminal matters was signed as per the cabinet meeting held on 16 October 2025 in the presence of Anil Kumar Sinha, Minister for Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. The agreement is expected to formally pave the way for cooperation and exchange of matters such as the collection and exchange of evidence during the investigation, prosecution, and judicial proceedings of criminal cases between the concerned authorities of both countries.

The agreement is expected to make a significant contribution to enabling the rule of law and enhancing institutional coordination in the judicial administration. With the implementation of the agreement, collaboration between the central authorities of both countries will become even stronger and more results-oriented.

The agreement serves as a milestone in reducing fiduciary crimes in Nepal and making investigation, prosecution, and justice delivery more effective. The agreement is also expected to further assist in mutual assessments related to the prevention of money laundering and terrorist financing. The ceremony was attended by the Ministry Secretary Parashwor Dhungana and representatives from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

full_article:
Kathmandu. Nepal Rastra Bank has determined the foreign exchange rate for today (Monday). Accordingly, the purchase rate for one US dollar has been set at 152 rupees 04 paisa and the selling rate at 152 rupees 64 paisa.

The purchase rate for one Australian dollar is 107 rupees 46 paisa and the selling rate is 107 rupees 89 paisa, and for one Canadian dollar, the purchase rate is 109 rupees 06 paisa and the selling rate is 109 rupees 49 paisa.

The purchase rate for one European Euro is 175 rupees 74 paisa and the selling rate is 176 rupees 43 paisa, and for one UK Pound Sterling, the purchase rate is 205 rupees 13 paisa and the selling rate is 205 rupees 94 paisa.

The central bank has stated that this exchange rate can be revised at any time as needed. The exchange rate set by commercial banks may differ, and the updated exchange rate will be available on the central bank's 'website'.

title: Nepal Drugs Limited recovers from 25-year crisis, targets 98 free medicines - The Rising Nepal
description: Nepal Drugs Limited recovers from 25-year crisis, targets 98 free medicines  The Rising Nepal

By Raman Paudel

Kathmandu, Aug. 10 : Nepal Drugs Limited, which had been closed for a decade, has now returned to profitability.

According to officials at Nepal Drugs Limited, the company is about to distribute at least 22 types of its own medicines to the market in large volumes within the next two months.

Kailash Kumar Paneru, General Manager of the company, said the industry achieved the World Health Organization’s Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) standard last year and has become profitable as both production and sales have increased.

“When I came to the company three years ago, the company had outstanding payments to the provident fund and other institutions. Now, it is not only profitable, but this year we have set a target of Rs. 300 million in turnover,” GM Paneru said.

The company, which sold medicines worth Rs. 120 million in 2001, last distributed bonuses to its employees in the same year and faced several challenges over the following 10 years.

In recent years, particularly after signing an MoU with Kathmandu Metropolitan City in 2025, the company has accelerated efforts to expand its market across the country. It later signed a second MoU with Bharatpur Metropolitan City.

According to Paneru, the company initially increased medicine production by signing an agreement with Kathmandu Metropolitan City, which helped it gain access to Provincial Supply Management Centres, local governments and federal hospitals.

The company has now reached agreements with six provinces, excluding Karnali. General Manager Paneru informed that the company has already signed MoUs with most of the municipalities in the Kathmandu Valley.

Recently, the federal government wrote to all local governments across the country asking them to purchase medicines from the company. This is also expected to expand its market across the country.“However, we have created a market not only among government bodies but also in the private sector,” GM Paneru said.

According to him, the company is currently producing 11 different types of medicines. Some are being produced at full capacity, while others are being produced at partial capacity. Production levels, however, will be determined based on market demand.

The company plans to produce 22 types of medicines, particularly essential drugs for conditions such as intestinal worms, diabetes, high blood pressure, thyroid disorders, and cholesterol, which are in high demand in the market. The government, however, has set a target for the company to produce 25 types of medicines.

Earlier, the company’s production was limited to medicines such as Cetaplus, Jeevan Jal and a few other products. Recently, however, the market has begun to expand as production increases, particularly in response to government demand. General Manager Paneru said the company’s presence in both the private market and government supply system has increased significantly.

After upgrading its plant and machinery to meet Good Manufacturing Practice (GM P) standards and obtaining GMP certification last year, the organization has focused its plans on expanding the production of essential medicines and supplying them through government-to-government (G2G) arrangements.

Paneru believes that once these medicines are introduced to the market, the industry’s income and profits will increase significantly. As a long-term goal, the industry has aimed to replace imports of essential medicines.

“The organization’s strategic role in public health security will increase by ensuring the supply of essential medicines such as Cetaplus and Jeevan Jal during disasters such as floods, landslides, COVID-19 and dengue outbreaks,” General Manager Paneru said.

He also claimed that the company is working with the aim of producing all 98 types of medicines that the government distributes free of cost within the next three years.

He expressed confidence that the company will develop into a model pharmaceutical industry in the future and be established as the state’s strategic drug repository.

He further said the process of purchasing the necessary raw materials is currently under way. Work is also under way to install the necessary automated machinery to convert the existing manual system into high-volume automated production and increase production capacity.

General Manager Paneru said preparations are also under way to recruit skilled technical manpower in accordance with the approved Organization and Management (O&M) survey.

Despite these achievements, the industry requires more infrastructure and human resources. “Although demand for medicines produced here has started to increase, there is still a shortage of equipment. The government has allocated a budget of Rs. 240 million in the current fiscal year. With the necessary equipment and additional manpower, we can produce 22 types of medicines,” he said.

How did the industry get into crisis?

The company, which once produced 114 types of medicines, was almost closed in 2007. When 375 employees became unemployed, problems also began to arise regarding the payment of salaries. According to an official, employees were forced to remain inactive for about 10 years.

Even three years ago, the company was facing a severe financial crisis. Employees had not received their regular salaries for three to four months.

An official at the company said it faced challenges for several reasons, including the fact that its medicines did not meet GMP standards.

“Earlier, the Department of Drugs Administration (DDA) had said that Nepal Drugs did not comply with GMP standards, and medicine production was stopped for 10 years. At that time, even though the reasons for non-compliance were identified, it was difficult for the company to operate due to the influence of private drug sellers. Officials at the Nepal Drugs were close to private sellers,” the official told The Rising Nepal on condition of anonymity.

The company, which had been facing various crises for 25 years, has returned to profitability after years of financial difficulties. The company recorded a loss of more than Rs. 100 million in fiscal year 2024/25 but managed to earn a profit of Rs. 30 million a year later, in fiscal year 2025/26.

General Manager Paneru said that after achieving GMP certification, it became easier for the company to pursue G2G arrangements with government agencies.

Govt gives priority to Nepal Drugs

The current government has prioritized Nepal Drugs Limited, which had previously received little state attention, and has emphasized expanding its production capacity. The company has also been included as a priority under the government’s 100-point governance reform programme led by Prime Minister Balendra Shah.

Under the programme, the government aims to gradually enable Nepal Drugs Limited to produce 98 types of free medicines within three years. The company is currently producing Jeevan Jal (ORS) sachets, Metronidazole 400 mg tablets and Cetirizine 10 mg tablets under its essential medicines category.

In addition, it is producing hemodialysis solutions (Part A and Part B), sanitizers, glycerin, Metronidazole DF tablets, Folic Acid 0.4 mg, distilled water, and Cetaplus under its non-essential medicines category.

महाप्रबंधक पनेरु नँ कहलकै, “बाढ़, भूस्खलन, कोविड-19 आरू डेंगू के प्रकोप जैसनौ आपदा के दौरान सेटाप्लस आरू जीवन जल जैसनौ आवश्यक दवाई के आपूर्ति सुनिश्चित करी क जनस्वास्थ्य सुरक्षा मँ संगठन के रणनीतिक भूमिका बढ़ी जैतै ।

महाप्रबंधक पनेरु नँ कहलकै कि मंजूर संगठन आरू प्रबंधन (ओ एंड एम) सर्वेक्षण के अनुसार कुशल तकनीकी जनशक्ति के भर्ती के तैयारी भी चलै छै ।

एहि उपलब्धि क बावजूद एहि उद्योग कए बेसी बुनियादी ढांचा आ मानव संसाधन क ​​जरूरत अछि। ओ कहला जे एतय उत्पादित दवाई क मांग भले बढ़य लागल अछि, मुदा एखनो उपकरण क कमी अछि, सरकार चालू वित्तीय वर्ष मे 24 करोड़ टका क बजट आवंटित केलक अछि। आवश्यक उपकरण आ अतिरिक्त जनशक्ति स हम 22 प्रकार क दवाई क उत्पादन क सकैत छी।'

उद्योग कोना संकट मे आबि गेल।

एक बेर 114 प्रकार क दवाई क उत्पादन करय वाला कंपनी 2007 मे लगभग बंद भ गेल छल।जखन 375 कर्मचारी बेरोजगार भ गेलाह त वेतन क भुगतान क संबंध मे सेहो समस्या पैदा होबय लागल। एकटा अधिकारी क अनुसार कर्मचारी कए करीब 10 साल तक निष्क्रिय रहबा लेल मजबूर कैल गेल।

तीन साल पहिने सेहो कंपनी कए भारी वित्तीय संकट क सामना करय पड़ल छल। तीन स चारि मास स कर्मचारी कए नियमित वेतन नहि भेटैत छल।

कंपनी क एकटा अधिकारी क कहब अछि जे ओकरा कईटा कारण स चुनौती क सामना करय पड़ैत अछि, जाहि मे इ तथ्य सेहो शामिल अछि जे ओकर दवाई जीएमपी मानक पर खरा नहि उतरैत अछि।

“पहिने औषधि प्रशासन विभाग (डीडीए) कहने छल जे नेपाल औषधि जीएमपी मानकक पालन नहि करैत अछि, आ दवाई उत्पादन १० वर्ष धरि बंद कएल गेल छल । ओहि समय अनुपालन नहि करबाक कारण क पहचान भ गेलाक बादो निजी दवाई बेचनिहार क प्रभाव क कारण कंपनी कए काज करब मुश्किल भ गेल छल। नेपाल ड्रग्स के अधिकारी निजी विक्रेता के करीबी छल।’ अधिकारी नाम नहि बताबय के शर्त पर द राइजिंग नेपाल के कहलनि।

25 साल स विभिन्न संकट क सामना करय वाला कंपनी सालों स आर्थिक कठिनाई क बाद मुनाफा मे वापस आबि गेल अछि। कंपनी कए 100 टका स बेसी क घाटा दर्ज कैल गेल। वित्तीय वर्ष 2024/25 मे 10 करोड़ टका देल गेल मुदा 10 करोड़ टका क मुनाफा कमाए मे सफल रहल। 3 करोड़ एक साल बाद, वित्तीय वर्ष 2025/26 मे।

महाप्रबंधक पनेरु नँ कहलकै कि जीएमपी प्रमाणीकरण हासिल करला के बाद कंपनी लेली सरकारी एजेंसी के साथ जी टू जी के व्यवस्था करना आसान होय गेलै ।

नेपाल ड्रग्स के प्राथमिकता देल गेल सरकार

वर्तमान सरकार नेपाल ड्रग्स लिमिटेड के प्राथमिकता देलक अछि, जेकरा पहिने राज्य के कम ध्यान देल गेल छल, आ उत्पादन क्षमता के विस्तार पर जोर देल गेल अछि. प्रधानमंत्री बलेन्द्र शाह के नेतृत्व मे सरकार के 100 सूत्री शासन सुधार कार्यक्रम के तहत सेहो कंपनी के प्राथमिकता के रूप मे शामिल कएल गेल अछि.

एहि कार्यक्रम के तहत सरकार के लक्ष्य अछि जे नेपाल ड्रग्स लिमिटेड के धीरे-धीरे तीन साल के भीतर 98 प्रकार के मुफ्त दवाई के उत्पादन करय मे सक्षम बनाबय के अछि. कंपनी एखन अपन आवश्यक दवाई श्रेणी मे जीवन जल (ओआरएस) पाउच, मेट्रोनिडाजोल 400 मिलीग्राम गोली आ सेटिरिजिन 10 मिलीग्राम गोली क उत्पादन क रहल अछि।

title: Susta residents building temporary embankment - The Rising Nepal
description: Susta residents building temporary embankment  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
By Our Correspondent

Parasi, Aug. 10: As erosion by the Narayani River intensifies, residents of Susta village in West Nawalparasi have begun efforts to protect their settlement using their own labour and locally available resources.

Although the tendering process for the construction of a permanent embankment had been completed, work was halted after it was reportedly obstructed from across the border, prompting local residents to build a temporary embankment.

As the river’s flow has begun to shift towards the settlement, residents of Susta, along with the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force, have been deployed to control the river. Temporary structures are being built in the eroded areas using sand-filled sacks, gabion wire mesh and tree branches.

Local residents are carrying sandbags and managing other materials through voluntary community labour. Security personnel are stationed along the riverbank and assisting efforts to control the erosion.

According to Rabindra Jaiswal, spokesperson for the Susta Protection Campaign, the tendering process for the construction of a permanent embankment to control the erosion had already been completed. However, the work could not proceed because of obstruction from the Indian side, he said.

“The construction of the permanent embankment, for which the contract has already been awarded, has been halted because of obstruction from the Indian side. As the risk of the river’s flow shifting towards the settlement has increased, we are now building a temporary embankment using local resources and voluntary community labour,” Jaiswal said.

Every year, erosion by the Narayani River puts farmland and settlements in Susta at risk. Although the river continues to erode the land annually, the failure to construct a permanent embankment has left local residents fearful during the monsoon.

As the erosion intensified, a team comprising federal lawmaker Bikram Khanal, Chief District Officer Dipak Raj Nepal and the heads of the district’s security agencies visited Susta for an on-site inspection. The team assessed the condition of the erosion-affected area and the potential risks.

During the inspection, Susta residents urged the authorities to immediately carry out temporary river-control measures to protect their homes, farmland and settlement from erosion, and to take initiatives for a long-term solution. They also called for the obstruction from across the border to be removed after the monsoon so that construction of the permanent embankment could proceed.

Khanal said necessary coordination was being carried out with the Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation to ensure the resources required for construction of the embankment.

CDO Nepal said the local administration, elected representatives and security agencies had been placed on high alert to minimise potential damage from erosion by the Narayani River. He said temporary control measures had been adopted for the time being and additional personnel would be mobilised according to the level of risk.

Every year, local residents have been contributing voluntary labour to protect their settlement and farmland from river erosion.

परासी, 10 अगस्त : नारायणी नदी के कटाव तेज होय के साथ-साथ पश्चिम नवलपरासी के सुस्ता गाँव के निवासी न॑ अपनऽ श्रम आरू स्थानीय रूप स॑ उपलब्ध संसाधन के उपयोग करी क॑ अपनऽ बस्ती के सुरक्षा के प्रयास शुरू करी देल॑ छै ।

हालांकि स्थायी तटबंध के निर्माण के निविदा प्रक्रिया पूरा भ गेल छल, मुदा सीमा पार स बाधा पहुंचला के बाद काज बंद भ गेल छल, जाहि स स्थानीय निवासी अस्थायी तटबंध बनेलथि।

नदी के बहाव बस्ती दिस बढ़य लागल अछि, एहि सं नदी पर नियंत्रण के लेल नेपाली सेना, नेपाल पुलिस आ सशस्त्र प्रहरी बल के संग सुस्ता के निवासी के तैनात कएल गेल अछि. कटाव वाला इलाका मे बालू सं भरल बोरा, गैबियन तार के जाली आ गाछ के डारि के उपयोग सं अस्थायी संरचना बनाओल जा रहल अछि.

स्थानीय निवासी स्वैच्छिक सामुदायिक श्रम के माध्यम स बालू के थैली ल क अन्य सामग्री के प्रबंधन क रहल छैथ। सुरक्षाकर्मी नदी के किनारे तैनात छै आरू कटाव क॑ नियंत्रित करै के प्रयास म॑ सहायता करी रहलऽ छै ।

सुस्ता संरक्षण अभियान के प्रवक्ता रवीन्द्र जायसवाल के अनुसार कटाव पर नियंत्रण के लेल स्थायी तटबंध के निर्माण के निविदा प्रक्रिया पूरा भ चुकल छल। मुदा भारतीय पक्ष स बाधा के कारण काज आगू नहि बढ़ि सकल ओ कहलनि।

जयसवाल कहलनि जे, स्थायी तटबंध के निर्माण, जकरा लेल ठेका पहिने सं देल जा चुकल अछि, भारतीय दिस सं बाधा के कारण बंद भ गेल अछि, जेना-जेना नदी के बहाव बस्ती दिस बढ़बाक खतरा बढ़ल अछि, हम सब आब स्थानीय संसाधन आ स्वैच्छिक सामुदायिक श्रम के उपयोग क अस्थायी तटबंध बना रहल छी।

हर साल नारायणी नदी केरऽ कटाव स॑ सुस्ता केरऽ खेती के जमीन आरू बस्ती खतरा म॑ पड़ै छै । हालांकि नदी सालाना जमीन कए कटाव जारी रखैत अछि, मुदा स्थायी तटबंध नहि बनेबा स मानसून क दौरान स्थानीय निवासी कए आतंकित भ गेल अछि।

कटाव तेज होइते संघीय विधायक बिक्रम खनाल, मुख्य जिल्ला अधिकारी दीपक राज नेपाल आ जिल्लाक सुरक्षा एजेन्सी प्रमुखसभक टोली स्थलगत निरीक्षणक लेल सुस्ता गेल छल । टीम कटाव प्रभावित क्षेत्र क स्थिति आ संभावित जोखिम क आकलन केलक।

निरीक्षण के दौरान सुस्ता के निवासी नँ अधिकारियौ स॑ आग्रह करलकै कि तुरंत अपनऽ घर, खेती के जमीन आरू बस्ती क॑ कटाव स॑ बचाबै लेली अस्थायी नदी-नियंत्रण उपाय करलऽ जाय, आरू एकरऽ दीर्घकालिक समाधान लेली पहल करलऽ जाय । संगहि मानसून के बाद सीमा पार स आबय वाला बाधा के हटाबय के आह्वान केलनि जाहि सं स्थायी तटबंध के निर्माण आगू बढ़ि सकय.

खनाल कहलनि जे, तटबंध निर्माण लेल आवश्यक संसाधन सुनिश्चित करबाक लेल ऊर्जा, जल संसाधन आ सिंचाई मंत्रालय के संग आवश्यक समन्वय कायल जा रहल अछि।

सीडीओ नेपाल कहलनि जे, नारायणी नदी द्वारा कटाव सँ संभावित क्षति कम सँ कम करबाक लेल स्थानीय प्रशासन, निर्वाचित प्रतिनिधि आ सुरक्षा निकाय केँ हाई अलर्ट मे राखल गेल अछि। ओ कहलनि जे, फिलहाल अस्थायी नियंत्रण के उपाय अपनाओल गेल अछि आ जोखिम के स्तर के हिसाब सं अतिरिक्त कर्मी के जुटाओल जायत।

हर साल स्थानीय निवासी अपन बस्ती आ खेती के जमीन के नदी के कटाव सं बचाबय लेल स्वैच्छिक श्रम के योगदान दैत आबि रहल छथिन्ह.

full_article:
By A Staff Reporter

Kathmandu, Aug. 10: President of the Nepal Olympic Committee, Jeevan Ram Shrestha, said that instability has hindered the progress and success that should have been achieved in Nepali sports.

Speaking at the seventh annual general assembly of the Nepal Ski Association on Sunday, President Shrestha stressed that if everyone works honestly within the legal framework, instability in sports can be overcome, enabling associations to confidently advance the development of sport.

He expressed optimism that recent changes in the country would bring positive transformation in the sports sector. “Ending uncertainty, instability, and interference would pave the way for sporting development and enhance national pride,” he said.

Shrestha, who is also the President of the Ski Association, stated that the Association is putting all its efforts into developing skiing in Nepal.

He noted that although not all intended goals have been achieved, every possible attempt is being made. “Despite Nepal being home to the Himalayas, including the world’s highest mountain, Mt Sagarmatha, winter sports remain little known in the nation,” he said. “If skiing can be developed, Nepal could become a destination for ski tourism,” Shrestha added.

Vice-President Rama Bhattarai thanked all those who have supported the promotion of the sport. General Secretary Bijaya Shrestha acknowledged the challenges of skiing in Nepal but affirmed that the Association is working to promote the sport as much as possible.

The inaugural ceremony was also addressed by Deepak Devkota, President of the Nepal Rugby Association; Pitambar Timilsina, President of the Nepal Handball Association; Chaturanan Rajvaidya, Vice-President of the NOC; Rajiv Shrestha, General Secretary of the NOC; and Dhan Shahi, representative of the National Sports Council.

During the event, the Association also unveiled Snowline, a magazine featuring ski activities and articles.

The closed session of the Association endorsed an annual budget of Rs. 34,808,800 for the fiscal year 2083–84. The budget has been allocated for organising national competitions, participating in international events, conducting training programmes, and preparing for the Winter Olympics.

The session also approved the work plan presented by Vice-President Rama Bhattarai, the annual report submitted by General Secretary Bijaya Shrestha, and the financial report presented by Treasurer Jitendra Shrestha.

Officials and members of the Ski Association participated both physically and virtually in the assembly. The Association’s new statute allows members unable to attend in person to join the assembly virtually.

काठमांडू, 10 अगस्त : नेपाल ओलम्पिक समितिक अध्यक्ष जीवन राम श्रेष्ठ नेपाली खेल मे जे प्रगति आ सफलता भेटबाक चाही छल ताहि मे अस्थिरता बाधित भेल बतौलनि ।

रविदिन नेपाल स्की संघके सातम वार्षिक आम सभामे बजैत राष्ट्रपति श्रेष्ठ जौं सब कियो कानूनी ढांचामे ईमानदारीसँ काज करए तऽ खेलमे अस्थिरता दूर कएल जा सकैत अछि, जाहिसँ संघ सभ आत्मविश्वाससँ खेलक विकासमे आगू बढि सकैत अछि ।

ओ आशा व्यक्त केलथि जे देश मे हाल मे आयल बदलाव स खेल क्षेत्र मे सकारात्मक परिवर्तन आओत। हुनी कहलकै, 'अनिश्चितता, अस्थिरता, आरू हस्तक्षेप के समाप्त करला स॑ खेल विकास के रास्ता खुलतै आरू राष्ट्रीय गौरव बढ़तै ।

स्की एसोसिएशन के अध्यक्ष सेहो रहल श्रेष्ठ नेपाल मे स्कीइंग के विकास मे अपन पूरा प्रयास लगा रहल बतौलनि ।

हुनी नोट करलकै कि भले ही सब इरादा के लक्ष्य पूरा नै होय सकलौ छै, लेकिन हर संभव प्रयास करलौ जाय रहलौ छै । ओ कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे विश्व के सबस ऊँच पहाड़ माउंट सागरमाथा सहित हिमालय के घर रहला के बावजूद शीतकालीन खेल के नाम राष्ट्र मे बहुत कम अछि। श्रेष्ठ कहलनि जे, जौं स्कीइंग के विकास भ सकैत अछि त नेपाल स्की पर्यटन के गंतव्य बनि सकैत अछि।

उपराष्ट्रपति रामा भट्टराई खेलके प्रचार प्रसार मे सहयोग देनिहार सब गोटेके धन्यवाद देलखिन । महासचिव विजया श्रेष्ठ नेपाल मे स्कीइंग के चुनौती के स्वीकार केलनि मुदा संघ एहि खेल के यथासंभव बढ़ावा देबय लेल काज क रहल अछि से पुष्टि केलनि।

उद्घाटन समारोहमे नेपाल रग्बी संघके अध्यक्ष दीपक देवकोटा; नेपाल हैण्डबॉल संघके अध्यक्ष पीताम्बर तिमिलसिना डा. चतुरानन राजवैद्य, एनओसी के उपाध्यक्ष, प्रो. राजीव श्रेष्ठ, एनओसी के महासचिव, प्रो. एवं राष्ट्रीय खेल परिषद के प्रतिनिधि धन शाही।

ई आयोजन के दौरान एसोसिएशन न॑ स्नोलाइन नाम केरऽ पत्रिका के अनावरण भी करलकै, जेकरा म॑ स्की गतिविधि आरू लेख शामिल छै ।

एसोसिएशन के बंद सत्र में 1000 रुपया के वार्षिक बजट के समर्थन कायल गेल। वित्तीय वर्ष 2083-84 के लिये 34,808,800 रुपये। ई बजट राष्ट्रीय प्रतियोगिता के आयोजन, अंतर्राष्ट्रीय आयोजनऽ म॑ भाग लेबै, प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रम के संचालन, आरू शीतकालीन ओलंपिक के तैयारी लेली आवंटित करलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

सत्रमे उपाध्यक्ष राम भट्टराई द्वारा प्रस्तुत कार्ययोजना, महासचिव विजय श्रेष्ठ द्वारा प्रस्तुत वार्षिक प्रतिवेदन, आ कोषाध्यक्ष जितेन्द्र श्रेष्ठ द्वारा प्रस्तुत वित्तीय प्रतिवेदनके अनुमोदन सेहो कएल गेल अछि ।

स्की एसोसिएशन केरऽ अधिकारी आरू सदस्य न॑ ई सभा म॑ शारीरिक आरू वर्चुअल दोनों तरह स॑ भाग लेलकै । एसोसिएशन केरऽ नया विधान म॑ व्यक्तिगत रूप स॑ उपस्थित नै होय वाला सदस्यऽ क॑ वर्चुअल रूप स॑ विधानसभा म॑ शामिल होय के अनुमति देलऽ गेलऽ छै ।

full_article:
Many people have heard about antibiotics, but do not precisely know what this medicine is and how it works, let alone what antimicrobial resistance (AMR) means. Yet, many have wondered why some infections become difficult to treat, even when antimicrobials are available. Do antimicrobials always work against infections? The fact remains that infectious agents, such as bacteria, do spontaneously develop resistance over time. But this process can be accelerated when bacteria are repeatedly exposed to antimicrobials, including through unnecessary or inappropriate use.

For the past several years, studies have consistently shown that Nepal, like other South Asian countries, experiences excessive and inappropriate use of antimicrobials. In urban areas, one can easily walk into a drug shop, explain symptoms and buy antibiotics, often without a prescription. A patient with a common cold may demand antibiotics even though antibiotics do not work against viruses.

But this is only one side of Nepal’s story. Travel to remote areas, and the problem may be the opposite. For populations in far-flung villages, access to even basic and essential antimicrobials can be difficult. A bacterial infection that could have been treated relatively easily could become severe and complicated. By the time the patient reaches a hospital, treatment can be more complicated and much more expensive.

This is the tension between access and excess. In one place, antimicrobials are easily available and consumed unnecessarily; in another, people who genuinely need them struggle to obtain them. Here lies the unsettling heterogeneity of who becomes vulnerable and who does not, and who needs attention and who, relatively, does not. This is the first premise where community engagement can offer solutions.

Such contradictions in Nepal’s supply side and demand side cannot simply be fixed by bombarding people with recommendations about ‘appropriate antibiotic use’. In such scenarios, stakeholder analysis allows one to explore a multitude of interests and their interactions, understand why people behave as they do, and analyse how health systems, pharmacies, patients, farmers and communities function within their own circumstances and in relation to each other. This is the second premise where community engagement can help resolve the puzzle.

Yet, engagement strategies have sometimes been given unequal weight, particularly with a preference for participatory and dialogue-based activities over approaches that prioritise breadth of engagement. In practice, however, both approaches can and need to coexist, often complementing each other.

Historically, experts developed recommendations at the centre, bureaucracies converted them into programmes, and instructions travelled downward through the health system until they eventually reached communities. Nepal is familiar with this model where a guideline is prepared in Kathmandu, training is provided at the provincial or district level, posters reach health facilities, and communities are told what behaviour should change. Inadequate community buy-in as such can undermine the entire effort.

The one-way nature of vertical engagement has also been rightly criticised. Experts and bureaucrats may prescribe solutions for communities whose everyday experiences are radically different from their own. Recommendations can be technically sound and well-intentioned but also poorly grounded and unrealistic. Imagine telling a person in a remote village that antibiotics must only be taken after consulting a qualified doctor when reaching that doctor requires a day’s walk and considerable expense. Or telling a small poultry farmer to simply reduce antimicrobial use without discussing veterinary access, disease prevention and the possibility that losing chickens may mean losing the household’s income.

Participatory engagement has enormous value. Community members can be involved from the outset, contribute to identifying problems, setting agendas, designing interventions, implementing activities, and evaluating results. Such involvement can garner trust, ownership and produce interventions grounded in local realities. Patients may explain why they avoid health facilities. Farmers may describe why antimicrobials are important for protecting their livestock. These conversations can reveal problems that an expert sitting in Kathmandu may never see.

But enthusiasm for deep participation should not lead us to undervalue another dimension of engagement—breadth. Nepal’s experience with vaccination, mass drug administration and public health campaigns demonstrates the value of reaching hundreds of thousands, sometimes millions, of people. Radio, television, schools, social media, health facilities and community networks can carry simple messages about antibiotics across enormous populations.

Such breadth-based engagement may lack the depth of a small participatory meeting, but its scale is precisely the strength. A community dialogue involving 30 people can uncover why antibiotics are misused in one municipality. A nationwide radio campaign can make hundreds of thousands think twice before demanding antibiotics for a viral cold. Why must one be considered inherently superior to the other?

This is precisely where diagonal community engagement becomes useful. It combines vertical, population-wide strategies with bottom-up, participatory and dialogue-based engagement. This is particularly relevant for Nepal as it is efficient for low- and middle-income countries. AMR is a super-wicked problem. It involves human health, animal health, agriculture, food systems, pharmacies, hospitals, sanitation, environmental contamination, regulation, economics and human behaviour. There will never be one community, one message or one intervention capable of addressing all these dimensions.

Nepal therefore needs engagement that can travel in both directions. Scientific evidence, surveillance, regulation and national communication must move outward from institutions to communities. At the same time, experiences, constraints and solutions emerging from communities must travel back towards policymakers and researchers. Health governance, in other words, should re-orient the approach to reap benefits from a combination of conventional vertical and more recent participatory approaches.

For AMR control, while relevant to many other public health interventions, the idea is to blend these approaches to reach millions at scale and listen deeply to socio-cultural features while identifying and safeguarding vulnerabilities.

बहुत लोग एंटीबायोटिक दवाइयक कें बारे मे सुनने छै, मुदा इ ठीक सं पता नहि छै की इ दवाई की छै आ इ कोना काज करएयत छै, एंटीमाइक्रोबियल रेजिस्टेंस (AMR) कें मतलब त दूर कें बात छै. तइयो बहुतो कें ई सवाल उठल छै कि किछ संक्रमण कें इलाज मुश्किल कियैक भ जायत छै, भले ही रोगाणुरोधी दवाई उपलब्ध होय छै. की रोगाणुरोधी दवाइयक हमेशा संक्रमण कें खिलाफ काज करएयत छै? तथ्य इ छै कि संक्रामक एजेंट, जेना बैक्टीरिया, समय कें साथ अनायास प्रतिरोधक क्षमता जरूर पैदा करएयत छै. मुदा इ प्रक्रिया तखन तेज भ सकएय छै जखन बैक्टीरिया बेर-बेर रोगाणुरोधी दवाइयक कें संपर्क मे आएल होयत छै, जइ मे अनावश्यक या अनुचित उपयोग कें माध्यम सं सेहो शामिल छै.

पिछला कई साल स अध्ययन स लगातार पता चलल अछि जे नेपाल मे सेहो दक्षिण एशिया क अन्य देश क तरह रोगाणुरोधी दवाई क अत्यधिक आ अनुचित उपयोग होइत अछि । शहरी क्षेत्रक मे, कोनों व्यक्ति आसानी सं दवाक कें दोकान मे घुस सकएय छै, लक्षणक कें समझा सकएय छै आ एंटीबायोटिक दवाइयक खरीद सकएय छै, अक्सर बिना पर्चे कें. आम सर्दी कें रोगी एंटीबायोटिक दवाइयक कें मांग कयर सकएय छै, भले ही एंटीबायोटिक दवाइयक वायरस कें खिलाफ काज नहि करएयत छै.

मुदा ई नेपालक कथाक एकटा पक्ष मात्र अछि । सुदूर इलाका मे यात्रा करू, आ समस्या एकर उल्टा भ सकैत अछि। दूरस्थ गामक मे आबादी कें लेल बेसिक आ आवश्यक रोगाणुरोधी दवाइयक कें पहुंच सेहो मुश्किल भ सकएय छै. बैक्टीरिया कें संक्रमण जेकर इलाज अपेक्षाकृत आसानी सं कैल जा सकएय छै, गंभीर आ जटिल भ सकएय छै. जाबे तइक रोगी अस्पताल पहुंचएयत छै, ओकर इलाज बेसि जटिल भ सकएय छै आ बहुत बेसि महग भ सकएय छै.

ई पहुँच आ अतिरिक्त के बीच के तनाव छै. एक ठाम रोगाणुरोधी दवाई आसानी सं भेटैत अछि आ अनावश्यक सेवन भ जाइत अछि ; दोसर मे जिनका एकर सच्चा जरूरत छनि ओ लोक एकरा प्राप्त करबा लेल संघर्ष करैत छथि । एतय ई अशांत विषमता निहित अछि जे के कमजोर भ जाइत अछि आ के नहि, आ केकरा ध्यान देबय के जरूरत अछि आ केकरा, अपेक्षाकृत, नहिं. इ पहिल आधार छै जत समुदायक कें जुड़ाव समाधान पेश कयर सकय छै.

नेपाल केरऽ आपूर्ति पक्ष आरू मांग पक्ष म॑ ऐसनऽ विरोधाभास क॑ खाली ‘उचित एंटीबायोटिक उपयोग’ के बारे म॑ सिफारिशऽ स॑ लोगऽ प॑ बमबारी करी क॑ ठीक नै करलऽ जाब॑ सकै छै । ऐहन परिदृश्यक मे हितधारक विश्लेषण कें अनुमति देयत छै की एकटा अनेक रुचि आ ओकर बातचीत कें खोज कैल जा सकय छै, इ समझल जा सकय छै की लोग ओय तरह कें व्यवहार कियाक करय छै, आ विश्लेषण करय सकय छै की स्वास्थ्य प्रणाली, दवाई कें दुकानक, मरीज, किसान आ समुदाय अपन परिस्थितिक कें भीतर आ एक दोसर कें संबंध मे कोना काज करय छै. इ दोसर आधार छै जतय सामुदायिक जुड़ाव पहेली कें हल करय मे मदद कयर सकय छै.

तइयो, संलग्नता रणनीतिक कें कखनो-कखनो असमान वजन देल गेल छै, विशेष रूप सं भागीदारी कें व्यापकता कें प्राथमिकता देवय वाला दृष्टिकोणक कें बजाय भागीदारी आ संवाद आधारित गतिविधियक कें प्राथमिकता देल गेल छै. मुदा व्यवहार मे दुनू दृष्टिकोण सह-अस्तित्व मे रहि सकैत अछि आ जरूरत अछि, जे प्रायः एक दोसराक पूरक होइत अछि ।

ऐतिहासिक रूप स॑ विशेषज्ञ न॑ केंद्र म॑ सिफारिश विकसित करलकै, नौकरशाही ओकरा कार्यक्रम म॑ बदली देलकै, आरू निर्देश स्वास्थ्य प्रणाली के माध्यम स॑ नीचें के तरफ यात्रा करलकै जब॑ तलक कि अंततः समुदाय तलक नै पहुँची गेलै । नेपाल एहि मॉडल स परिचित अछि जतय काठमांडू मे दिशा निर्देश तैयार कैल जाइत अछि, प्रांतीय या जिला स्तर पर प्रशिक्षण देल जाइत अछि, स्वास्थ्य सुविधा तक पोस्टर पहुंचैत अछि, आ समुदाय कए कहल जाइत अछि जे कोन व्यवहार मे बदलाव हेबाक चाही। अपर्याप्त सामुदायिक खरीद-इन जेना कि पूरा प्रयास कें कमजोर कयर सकय छै.

ऊर्ध्वाधर जुड़ाव के एकतरफा प्रकृति के भी सही आलोचना करलऽ गेलऽ छै । विशेषज्ञ आ नौकरशाह ओय समुदायक कें लेल समाधान निर्धारित कयर सकय छै, जेकर रोजमर्रा कें अनुभव ओकर अनुभव सं मौलिक रूप सं भिन्न छै. सिफारिश तकनीकी रूप सं सही आ नीक नीयत सं भ सकैत अछि मुदा खराब जमीनी आ अवास्तविक सेहो भ सकैत अछि. कल्पना करू जे कोनो सुदूर गाम मे कोनो व्यक्ति केँ ई कहब जे एंटीबायोटिक दवाई योग्य डॉक्टर सँ सलाह लेलाक बाद मात्र सेवन करय पड़त जखन ओहि डाक्टर लग पहुँचबा मे एक दिनक पैदल यात्रा आ काफी खर्चा करय पड़ैत छैक. या कोनों छोट मुर्गी पालन करय वाला कें कहनाय की पशु चिकित्सा पहुंच, बीमारी रोकथाम आ इ संभावना कें चर्चा करएय कें बिना बस रोगाणुरोधी दवाइयक कें उपयोग कें कम करएय कें लेल की मुर्गी कें नुकसान कें मतलब घरक कें आमदनी कें नुकसान भ सकएय छै.

सहभागी जुड़ाव के अपार मूल्य छै। समुदाय कें सदस्यक कें शुरु आत सं शामिल कैल जा सकएय छै, समस्याक कें पहचान करएय मे, एजेंडा तय करएय मे, हस्तक्षेपक कें डिजाइन करएय मे, गतिविधियक कें लागू करएय मे, आ परिणामक कें मूल्यांकन करएय मे योगदान द सकएय छै. ऐहन संलग्नता विश्वास, स्वामित्व जुटा सकय छै आ स्थानीय वास्तविकताक पर आधारित हस्तक्षेप पैदा कयर सकय छै. मरीज इ बता सकएय छै की ओ स्वास्थ्य सुविधाक सं बचएयत छै. किसानक इ वर्णन कयर सकय छै की ओकर पशुधन कें सुरक्षा कें लेल रोगाणुरोधी दवाइयक कें महत्व कियाक छै. एहि गप्प-सप्प स एहन समस्या सामने आबि सकैत अछि जे काठमांडू मे बैसल कोनो विशेषज्ञ कए शायद कहियो नहि देखबा मे आबि सकैत अछि।

मुदा गहींर सहभागिता के उत्साह हमरा सब के सगाई के एकटा आओर आयाम-व्यापकता के कम करय लेल नहिं ल' जेबाक चाही. नेपाल केरऽ टीकाकरण, सामूहिक औषधि प्रशासन आरू जनस्वास्थ्य अभियान केरऽ अनुभव लाखों, कखनी-कखनी लाखों लोगऽ तलक पहुँचै के मूल्य क॑ दर्शाबै छै । रेडियो, टेलीविजन, स्कूल, सोशल मीडिया, स्वास्थ्य सुविधाक आ सामुदायिक नेटवर्क विशाल आबादी मे एंटीबायोटिक दवाइयक कें बारे मे सरल संदेश पहुंचा सकय छै.

ऐन्हऽ व्यापकता आधारित जुड़ाव म॑ छोटऽ भागीदारी वाला बैठक के गहराई के कमी होय सकै छै, लेकिन एकरऽ पैमाना ठीक ताकत छै । 30 लोगक कें शामिल सामुदायिक संवाद सं पता चल सकय छै कि एकटा नगरपालिका मे एंटीबायोटिक कें दुरुपयोग कियाक कैल जायत छै. देशव्यापी रेडियो अभियान लाखों लोगऽ क॑ वायरल सर्दी लेली एंटीबायोटिक दवाई के मांग करै स॑ पहल॑ दू बार सोचै लेली मजबूर करी सकै छै । एकटा के दोसर स स्वाभाविक रूप स श्रेष्ठ किएक मानल जेबाक चाही?

ठीक यही ठाम तिरछा सामुदायिक जुड़ाव उपयोगी भ जायत छै. इ ऊर्ध्वाधर, जनसंख्या-व्यापी रणनीतियक कें साथ नीचा सं ऊपर, सहभागी आ संवाद आधारित जुड़ाव कें संयोजन करयत छै. ई नेपाल के लेलऽ विशेष रूप स॑ प्रासंगिक छै, कैन्हेंकि ई कम आरू मध्यम आय वाला देशऽ लेली कुशल छै । एएमआर एकटा सुपर-दुष्ट समस्या अछि। एहि मे मानव स्वास्थ्य, पशु स्वास्थ्य, कृषि, खाद्य प्रणाली, फार्मेसी, अस्पताल, स्वच्छता, पर्यावरण प्रदूषण, नियमन, अर्थशास्त्र आ मानव व्यवहार शामिल अछि । एहि सब आयाम कए संबोधित करबा मे सक्षम कहियो एकटा समुदाय, एकटा संदेश या एकटा हस्तक्षेप नहि होएत।

एहि लेल नेपाल के एहन सगाई के जरूरत अछि जे दुनू दिशा मे यात्रा क सकय. वैज्ञानिक साक्ष्य, निगरानी, ​​नियमन आ राष्ट्रीय संचार कें संस्थाक सं समुदायक मे बाहर दिस बढ़नाय आवश्यक छै. एकरऽ साथ ही समुदायऽ स॑ निकलै वाला अनुभव, बाधा आरू समाधान क॑ नीति निर्माता आरू शोधकर्ता के तरफ वापस जाय के जरूरत छै । स्वास्थ्य शासन कें, दोसर शब्दक मे, पारंपरिक ऊर्ध्वाधर आ बेसि हाल कें भागीदारी वाला दृष्टिकोण कें संयोजन सं लाभ उठावा कें लेल दृष्टिकोण कें पुनः उन्मुख करबाक चाही.

एएमआर नियंत्रण कें लेल, जखन कि बहुत सं अन्य जनस्वास्थ्य हस्तक्षेपक कें लेल प्रासंगिक छै, विचार इ छै की इ दृष्टिकोणक कें मिश्रण कैल जै ताकि पैमाना पर लाखक कें बीच पहुंचल जा सकय आ सामाजिक-सांस्कृतिक विशेषताक कें गहराई सं सुनल जा सकय आ जखन कि कमजोरी कें पहचान कैल जा सकय आ ओकर सुरक्षा कैल जा सकय.
